correctness.rationale: For centered isotropic X in R^d with exactly m=d+1 positive-probability atoms, weighted Gram projection gives v_i·v_j=δ_ij/p_i−1, realizing every strictly positive mass profile up to orthogonal equivalence. Directions correspond isometrically to weighted mean-zero variance-one scalar profiles. Lagrange multiplier stationarity for cubic skewness has two levels, and the minimum atomic mass q controls the sharp K=(1−2q)/sqrt(q(1−q)), attained at a singleton-minimal-atom direction. Completeness of {1,X_1,...,X_d} in L²(p) gives T-Hilbert identity H²=E||X||^4−d=sum_i1/p_i−3(d+1)+2. Fixing q reduces possible H² to convex reciprocal sum on p_i>=q; Jensen gives lower and vertices upper, and a continuous path realizes every intermediate value. This yields bounds 1/q+d²/(1−q)−3d−1 and d/q+1/(1−dq)−3d−1, extremal profiles and χ² identity. Finite-support characteristic-function Taylor expansion gives the stated iid Brownian weak-Fourier leading coefficient only; not a general scheme lower bound. Independent exact Gram/tensor/endpoint checks covered six rational profiles; proof is analytic for all d>=2.
residual_risks: The independent finite checks are bounded and do not themselves establish infinite quantifiers.

Tanaka 2026 states qualitative noncancellation and Fourier barrier, without the full two-norm interval. Published Resultary Endpoint masses determine the exact skewness range of a discrete law covers the one-dimensional two-level scalar skewness optimization underlying K, explicitly not claimed as new on its own. The residual proposed contribution is the exact joint spectral/Frobenius feasible region and extremizer classification. None of inspected sources implies both norm extrema at fixed K. Potential older obtuse-variable fourth-moment inequality remains a priority risk.
